events.blurb: Emperor Frederick Barbarossa summons the northern Italian cities to the Diet of Roncaglia and asserts sweeping imperial rights over them, including taxation and the appointment of city officials. The cities resist, and the conflict hardens into the Guelph-Ghibelline divide: the Guelphs backing the pope, the Ghibellines the emperor.
events.label: Diet of Roncaglia, 1158

events.blurb: After years of defiance, Barbarossa takes Milan and razes it, scattering its people. The destruction becomes the founding grievance of the Lombard League.
events.label: Milan razed, 1162

events.blurb: The cities of Lombardy swear the Lombard League against the emperor, pooling their armies and revenues to defend communal self-government.
events.label: Lombard League formed, 1167

events.blurb: The Lombard League's infantry, dug in around its carroccio, holds against Barbarossa's knights at Legnano, and the regrouped League cavalry routs the imperial army. The victory saves the communes and forces the emperor to negotiate.
events.label: Legnano, 1176

events.blurb: The Peace of Constance confirms the Lombard cities' rights to elect their consuls and govern themselves, in exchange for recognizing imperial overlordship. The communes survive as self-governing states inside the empire.
events.label: Peace of Constance, 1183

events.blurb: Emperor Frederick II crushes the Lombard League's army at Cortenuova, capturing the carroccio itself. It is the high-water mark of Hohenstaufen power in northern Italy.
events.label: Cortenuova, 1237

events.blurb: Parma's defenders sally out and sack Frederick II's siege camp, capturing his treasure and crown. The defeat breaks the emperor's grip on Lombardy, and he dies two years later.
events.label: Parma turns the tide, 1248

events.blurb: Florence's Guelph army is annihilated by Siena's Ghibellines at Montaperti. Florence falls to the Ghibellines, and the battle lives on in Dante's poem.
events.label: Montaperti, 1260

events.blurb: Charles of Anjou, granted the Sicilian crown by the pope, defeats and kills Manfred, Frederick II's son, at Benevento. A French Angevin dynasty takes Naples and Sicily, and the Guelphs triumph in the south.
events.label: Benevento, 1266

events.blurb: Conradin, the last Hohenstaufen claimant, is defeated at Tagliacozzo and beheaded at Naples on Charles of Anjou's orders. Hohenstaufen rule in Italy ends.
events.label: Tagliacozzo, 1268

events.blurb: On Easter Monday in Palermo, a revolt against Angevin officials explodes into a massacre of the French. Peter III of Aragon lands in support of the rebels, and the War of the Sicilian Vespers splits the island from Naples for good.
events.label: Sicilian Vespers, 1282

events.blurb: The Peace of Caltabellotta ends twenty years of war over Sicily: the island goes to Aragon, Naples stays Angevin. The split between the Two Sicilies lasts until the nineteenth century.
events.label: Peace of Caltabellotta, 1302

events.blurb: Gian Galeazzo Visconti, who had nearly united northern Italy under Milan, dies of plague at Melegnano. His empire collapses into succession chaos, and the peninsula's balance resets.
events.label: Visconti's empire collapses, 1402

events.blurb: Venice, Milan, Florence, Naples, and the Papal States sign the Peace of Lodi, freezing Italy's borders and creating a balance-of-power system that holds, more or less, for forty years.
events.label: Peace of Lodi, 1454

events.blurb: Charles VIII of France invades with 25,000 men and a mobile siege train that shatters city walls in days. He marches the length of Italy and takes Naples, ending the Lodi balance and opening sixty-five years of foreign war over the peninsula.
events.label: Charles VIII invades, 1494

events.blurb: The League of Venice tries to cut off Charles VIII's retreat at Fornovo. The French fight through and escape, but the invasion has taught every European power that Italy is up for grabs.
events.label: Fornovo, 1495

events.blurb: Louis XII's French army seizes Milan and deposes the Sforza. Ludovico il Moro's fall ends Milan's independence and makes Lombardy a French-Spanish battleground.
events.label: France takes Milan, 1499

events.blurb: Spanish troops under Gonzalo de Córdoba win at the Garigliano, securing Naples for Spain. Southern Italy passes under Spanish rule for the next two centuries.
events.label: Garigliano, 1503

events.blurb: Pope Julius II's League of Cambrai turns on Venice, and a French army crushes the Venetians at Agnadello. Venice loses its mainland empire in a single day and spends years clawing it back.
events.label: Agnadello, 1509

events.blurb: The French destroy a Spanish army at Ravenna but lose their commander, Gaston de Foix, in the pursuit. The costly victory marks the turn of the wars against France.
events.label: Ravenna, 1512

events.blurb: Francis I crushes the Swiss pikemen defending Milan at Marignano, recovering the duchy for France. The battle ends Swiss expansion and makes Francis the arbiter of northern Italy.
events.label: Marignano, 1515

events.blurb: Imperial troops rout the French at La Bicocca, where Spanish arquebusiers behind earthworks slaughter the advancing Swiss. The battle announces the dominance of gunpowder infantry.
events.label: La Bicocca, 1522

events.blurb: Imperial forces annihilate the French at Pavia and capture Francis I himself. The king signs the Treaty of Madrid renouncing French claims in Italy, though he repudiates it once free.
events.label: Pavia, 1525

events.blurb: Unpaid imperial troops, many of them Lutheran Landsknechte, storm Rome and sack it for months. The Sack breaks the High Renaissance, humiliates the papacy, and drives Clement VII into the emperor's camp.
events.label: Sack of Rome, 1527

events.blurb: The Treaty of Cateau-Cambrésis ends the Italian Wars: France keeps Calais and a few fortresses but abandons Italy, and Spain emerges as the peninsula's dominant power for a century and a half.
events.label: Cateau-Cambrésis, 1559

events.blurb: The Holy League fleet, led by Don John of Austria with a large Venetian contingent, destroys the Ottoman fleet at Lepanto. It is the last great galley battle in history and halts Ottoman expansion in the western Mediterranean.
events.label: Lepanto, 1571

events.blurb: Imperial troops sack Mantua during the War of the Mantuan Succession, and plague follows the armies into the city. Mantua never recovers its Renaissance splendor.
events.label: Sack of Mantua, 1630

events.blurb: Charles II of Spain dies childless, bequeathing his empire to Philip of Anjou, grandson of Louis XIV. The succession crisis will plunge Europe into another war over Italy and Spain.
events.label: Charles II of Spain dies, 1700
